messages:
maya: Quick question—should the first-run helper be a tiny persistent ‘Need help?’ strip in the top-right (always visible) or an invisible context-aware guide that only shows inline hints when user pauses?
chris: my gut says persistent strip for discoverability, esp for non-technical folks. less surprise. :+1:
anita: accessibility note: persistent controls are easier for keyboard & screen reader users to find. invisible hints often never get keyboard focus.
leo: downside is persistent strip eats UI real estate on small screens. we could collapse to an icon that expands.
sarah: copy perspective—if it's persistent we need microcopy that doesn't scream "tour". something friendly: "Quickstart helper" vs "Need help?". preferences?
maya: thinking: "Quickstart helper" feels product-y. "Need help?" feels like support. maybe "Get started"?
chris: +1 to "Get started". Short and action oriented.
anita: for SR users, the button should have aria-label="Open onboarding helper, keyboard shortcut G then H" (if we add shortcut). Also we should expose it in the "Help" landmark.
leo: implementation: we can make the strip a small 40px pill fixed in the corner, expand to a panel when clicked. panel contains checklist, sample projects, and a small "import own project" CTA.
sarah: checklist copy draft: 1) Create API key 2) Run first request 3) Try sample app 4) Set billing limit. each item short and with status indicator. thoughts?
maya: love the checklist. can we put the sample projects above billing? lower friction first.
chris: agree—ordering should be friction-first. sample projects give quick value. billing can be a follow-up nudge.
anita: a11y nit: status indicators need both color and text (e.g., "Complete", "Incomplete") and focusable toggles. color-only is a fail.
leo: tech note: we can preload tiny samples into client so opening panel is instant. size budget ~80KB gzipped per sample metadata.
sarah: copy tweak: change "Try sample app" to "Run sample app (1 click)" — sets expectation. but might be too wordy.
maya: maybe "Run sample app" and show spinner microcopy when running.
anita: keyboard flow: focus lands on the strip, Enter opens, first focus goes to the checklist. Escape closes. Tab cycles inside panel only. also ensure focus trap works for screen readers.
chris: debate: do we auto-surface inline contextual hints after user fails a step (e.g., API key missing)? or just leave troubleshooting in panel?
leo: we could do a hybrid: persistent strip + server-sent lightweight hints that appear inline only for the failing component. but we must throttle hints to avoid nagging.
anita: privacy/telemetry: any failure-triggered hint should be opt-in. need to mention in privacy banner if we send error telemetry.
sarah: design mock suggestion: small helper panel with two tabs: Quickstart (checklist + samples) and Troubleshoot (diagnostics with one-click fix suggestions). simple layout.
maya: can we get a quick Figma frame to compare persistent strip vs contextual-only? i'll drop a frame. :eyes:
design-bot: Figma link uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/onboard-helper-comps (preview mode).
chris: quick UX question—should sample projects open in the panel (embedded) or create a workspace page? I prefer embed for speed.
sarah: embed wins for first-run, but give a "Open full workspace" after they run it.
anita: contrast check: strip text must meet AA (4.5:1) on all background colors. dark mode baseline tests: label white on primary-blue passes at 4.8:1. checkbox icon states need 3:1 at minimum for touch targets.
leo: engineering follow-ups: 1) add keyboard shortcut discovery hint in product cmd palette 2) preload sample metadata 3) add server flag for rollout 4) telemetry event names: onboard.helper.open, onboard.sample.run, onboard.checklist.complete.
maya: rollout plan: canary to 10% of new accounts for 2 weeks, measure: time-to-first-sample-run, checklist completion rate, support messages asking how to onboard.
chris: success metric suggestion: target 30% checklist completion within first 7 days, + reduce first-week support tickets by 15%.
sarah: copy polish tasks for me: microcopy for button, checklist items, success toast, and one-liner for troubleshooting tab. I'll push PR with examples.
anita: I'll write accessibility acceptance criteria and a short keyboard walkthrough to include in the PR template.
leo: I'll add flags and basic telemetry. estimate ~3 dev days + 1 qa.
maya: thanks all—I'll create the Figma diff and a short prototype. tagging design-review next Wed. any last thoughts?
chris: just a tiny UX nit—when panel is open, page scroll shouldn't jump. use fixed positioning inside portal.
anita: also ensure the portal is announced to SR as a dialog: role=dialog and aria-modal=true.
maya: noted. putting these into the PR checklist now. :tada:
